package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a base64-encoded payload in setup.py that, when decoded, attempts to execute code on the victim's system to enable remote access or install a backdoor. The package is also likely part of a typosquatting campaign, attempting to trick users into installing it by mimicking the name of legitimate packages.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import base64
exec(base64.b64decode('...'))  # base64-encoded payload that, when decoded, attempts to download and execute code from hxxp://54[.]237[.]36[.]60/
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code decodes a base64-encoded payload and executes it, which attempts to download and execute a remote file from hxxp://54[.]237[.]36[.]60/, potentially enabling remote access or installing a backdoor.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Decoding and executing base64-encoded payloads during installation is a common obfuscation technique used by malware to hide its true intent and evade detection. The code attempts to contact an external server and execute whatever is returned, which is highly indicative of malicious behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal setup.py scripts should only handle package installation logic and should not execute obfuscated code or contact external servers to download and run additional payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may use base64 encoding for data serialization, but not for executing arbitrary code from remote sources during installation.
key_indicators: use of exec() on decoded data
network request to suspicious external IP

behavioral_signatures: Execution of base64-decoded payloads during package installation
Network requests to hardcoded external IPs or suspicious domains from setup.py
Use of exec() or eval() on dynamically decoded data in installation scripts
file_indicators: Obfuscated or encoded payloads in installation scripts
network_indicators: Connections to IPs or domains associated with game cheats or malware distribution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor installation scripts (setup.py) for the presence of base64 decoding and execution functions (e.g., exec(base64.b64decode(...))). Flag any package that attempts to contact external IPs or domains during installation, especially if the code is obfuscated or encoded. Use network monitoring to detect outbound requests to known malicious infrastructure such as hxxp://54[.]237[.]36[.]60/.
